purpose: Stage A final instruction v5, CLOSE-6D items 6B-1(a), 6B-1(b), 6B-1(c), 6B-4(c), 6B-5(a): the publisher's own published values, unrounded, as returned by the open API. No microdata; no API key.

notes.same_wave: The publisher files the low-income aggregate at year 2021 and Yemen's own observation at year 2022, within one survey wave (Yemen fieldwork November 2022 to January 2023); date=2021 returns no value for Yemen. Say 'the same survey wave', never 'the same year'.
notes.mobileaccount_LIC_not_published: 18.3073126606225 (mobileaccount.t.d, LIC, 2021) is NOT published by this resource. CauseWay's reconstruction of the publisher's aggregation (not a published statement): Yemen's missing mobile-money value enters the aggregate's numerator as zero while Yemen's adults stay in the denominator, so it is not a like-for-like comparator for Yemen and is a missing-is-not-zero problem inside the publisher's arithmetic. It stays here and in the Master, on no public page.
notes.fiaccount_LIC_comparator: fiaccount.t.d (24.4577497822049) is the publisher's own aggregate and the only one of the three that compares with Yemen's 11.9% on the same definition (account at a bank or similar financial institution).
notes.overlap_bound: CauseWay calculation from two published shares (not a published statistic): (fh2 31.9313981068809 - fiaccount.t.d 11.9033656433415) / 31.9313981068809 = 62.722066%, published as 'at least 62.7%' of adults who received domestic remittances did not have an account at a financial institution. A bound on the group; it does not establish the channel and does not rule out an account type the survey did not measure.
notes.fin22a: 0.4% is the Little Data Book 2015 (printed p.160) value for 2014; the current database gives 0.602877248196788 (0.6%) for fin22a 2014 and 1.79326303531445 (1.8%) for 2022. Comparisons of 2014 with 2022 use 0.6%.
notes.fin29_conflict: fin29 ('Received domestic remittances: into an account (% age 15+)') is 0 for Yemen at year 2022, with no value for fin29.s (% of recipients) or for the group series (fin29.1, fin29.2, fin29.7 read). The World Bank's published variable documentation for the same study (microdata catalog 5862, variable V67, fin29_1 'Received domestic remittances through an account') shows 393 valid answers and 39 'yes' (unweighted response counts; the item is asked of recipients). The published series is a share of all adults and its definition does not explain a printed 0. The two statements cannot both describe the same quantity; the printed value is not used and no reason is offered. The database (source 28) publishes no domestic-remittance series for cash or money-transfer operators: its channel series are fin28, fin28.29 and fin29 (account) and their .s variants (indicator list read 11 October 2026).
notes.lic_classification: api.worldbank.org/v2/sources/28/country/LIC/series/account.t.d/metadata, SpecialNotes: "The World Bank's FY24 classification is used, where low-income economies had a 2022 Atlas GNI per capita of $1,135 or less." No count of economies is stated for the aggregate (read 11 October 2026).
